title: Save and restore a text editor's state
description: TextEditor lets the user type text and supports undo via saved snapshots. Memento captures the editor's content at a point in time. History manages a stack of Mementos. Implement Memento, History, and TextEditor.save()/restore() so the editor can step back through previous states.
hints: Memento stores a single String — the content at the time of saving
History.push() saves a memento; History.pop() returns the most recent one (or null if empty)
TextEditor.save() creates a Memento of the current content; restore() sets content to the memento's saved value
issues: Without mementos, undo requires exposing internal state or maintaining it manually
Undo history couples the editor to its own past states
overallGoal: Use the Memento pattern so TextEditor can save snapshots of its content and restore them, with History acting as the caretaker.
goals: Create a Memento class that stores a snapshot of the editor's content
Implement save() to return a new Memento capturing the current content
Implement restore() to set the editor's content from a given Memento
Implement History as a LIFO stack that pushes on save and pops on undo
